document_title: All 245 Large Loads answered ERCOT, and cooling questions had the highest N/A rate
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Every Large Load answered ERCOT.

That is all 245 loads of 75 MW or greater. The count comes from a preliminary ERCOT summary for the utility commission's November 5th open meeting. In total 433 of 465 loads responded, covering about 177 GW. West Texas holds 41% of the capacity requested, 73 GW.

What went unanswered?

Respondents answered 83% of nearly 67,000 questions. Cooling questions drew N/A answers at the highest rate. Respondents indicated many projects had not determined their final cooling configuration. Projects asking to energize in 2028 or later answered N/A 30% more often than those due sooner.

ERCOT is targeting a published final report on December 10th.

Will the December 10th report count how many projects still haven't settled on cooling?

#ERCOT #PUCT #WestTexas

S1.headline: Answers cover about 177 GW. Cooling, often undecided.
S1.body: ERCOT sent its data center impact questions to 465 loads. In a preliminary summary to the utility commission on November 5th, cooling questions drew N/A answers at the highest rate.

ERCOT sent its data center impact questions to 465 loads. In a preliminary summary to the utility commission on November 5th, cooling questions drew N/A answers at the highest rate.

S2.headline: All 245 Large Loads answered
S2.body: Large Loads are 75 MW or greater and hold about 94% of the capacity requested. Among them, 33 projects ask for more than 1 GW each and represent 36% of capacity. One reel stands for one load, drawn to illustrate.
strings: Large Loads are 75 MW or greater and hold about 94% of the capacity requested. Among them, 33 projects ask for more than 1 GW each and represent 36% of capacity. One reel stands for one load, drawn to illustrate.

S3.headline: 433 of 465 answered
S3.body: The 433 that answered cover about 177 GW, about 97% of the capacity requested. 417 came in on time and 16 late, and 32 Medium Load responses had not arrived. One copper bar stands for one gigawatt, drawn to illustrate.
strings: The 433 that answered cover about 177 GW, about 97% of the capacity requested. 417 came in on time and 16 late, and 32 Medium Load responses had not arrived. One copper bar stands for one gigawatt, drawn to illustrate.

S4.headline: West Texas asked for 73 GW
S4.body: Every ERCOT load zone has requests, and West Texas holds 41% of the capacity. Zone figures cover 429 loads and leave out NOIE zones. A load's actual zone is set at interconnection and may differ.
strings: Every ERCOT load zone has requests, and West Texas holds 41% of the capacity. Zone figures cover 429 loads and leave out NOIE zones. A load's actual zone is set at interconnection and may differ.

S5.headline: 83% of the questions answered
S5.body: Respondents answered 83% of nearly 67,000 questions. N/A ran about 16% for Large Loads and 19% for Medium Loads. The open stretch is the share left unanswered, drawn to illustrate.
strings: Respondents answered 83% of nearly 67,000 questions. N/A ran about 16% for Large Loads and 19% for Medium Loads. The open stretch is the share left unanswered, drawn to illustrate.

S6.headline: Cooling had the highest N/A rate
S6.body: No category of questions drew N/A answers at a higher rate than cooling. Respondents indicated many projects had not determined their final cooling configuration.
strings: Cooling had the highest N/A rate
No category of questions drew N/A answers at a higher rate than cooling. Respondents indicated many projects had not determined their final cooling configuration.

S7.headline: Later projects said N/A more often
S7.body: Projects asking to energize in 2028 or later answered N/A 30% more often than those due sooner. The longer row of capped stubs stands for them, drawn to illustrate.
strings: Later projects said N/A more often
Projects asking to energize in 2028 or later answered N/A 30% more often than those due sooner. The longer row of capped stubs stands for them, drawn to illustrate.

S8.headline: ERCOT expects to go back to 80% of developers
S8.body: In a separate check of Batch Zero eligibility, ERCOT reviewed responses from 257 developers and expects to send 80% of them a second round, with a 5 business day deadline. Common issues so far include proving site control and confirming financial security posted.
strings: ERCOT expects to go back to 80% of developers

S9.headline: Final report targeted for December 10th
S9.body: ERCOT says detailed analysis is under way and targets a published final report on December 10th. The RFI figures are marked preliminary and subject to change.
